title: Permission activation windows and audit retention policy
content:
Summary
This note proposes a pragmatic approach for permission activation windows (time-limited grants), an accompanying audit retention policy optimized for SIEM ingestion, and an operational rollout checklist for RBAC v2. Purpose is to reduce blast radius from transient entitlements while preserving forensic fidelity for compliance and incident response.

Why this matters (context)
- We are expanding fine-grained, temporal entitlements for Dedicated and Private customers (supporting just-in-time capabilities, support scaffolding, and delegated troubleshooting).
- Temporal grants increase dynamicity of permissions, which improves safety but complicates auditability and SIEM exports unless TTLs and retention are standardized.
- Compliance teams require deterministic retention windows and searchable evidence for 90/180/365 day policies depending on region and regulator.

Goals
- Define standard activation-window semantics and how they appear in audit streams.
- Define an audit retention tiering model (hot / warm / cold / archive) and minimum retention by evidence type.
- Provide SIEM-friendly export shape and batching strategy to avoid spikes and rate limits.
- Provide a staged rollout/rollback plan with acceptance tests and sampling.

Scope
- Applies to RBAC v2 entitlements: time-bound role grants, ephemeral session tokens, delegated escalation tokens, and admin override windows.
- Covers server-side evidence generation, in-flight tagging, and SIEM export adapters. Does NOT cover KMS/HSM key rotation policies (separate doc).

Definitions (short)
- Activation window: the explicit start and end time for a granted entitlement (start_ts, end_ts).
- Entitlement epoch: a numbered change sequence for a user/role mapping at a point-in-time.
- Evidence snapshot: a compact record (event) that captures pre- and post-state and decision rationale for a change.
- Proof-of-exercise: optional addendum stored for high-risk actions (e.g., support session transcript, justification string).

Design proposal: Activation windows and evidence semantics
1) Canonical fields on entitlement-change events (must emit for every change):
   - event_id (uuid)
   - timestamp (ISO8601)
   - actor (service_account | user_id)
   - subject (user_id | service_id | tenant_id)
   - entitlement_type (role | permission | escalation_token)
   - previous_state (brief enum: none | bound | active | expired | revoked)
   - new_state (same enum)
   - activation_window_start (ISO8601 or null)
   - activation_window_end (ISO8601 or null)
   - reason (free text; max 1024 chars)
   - evidence_refs (list of pointers to stored snapshots or URLs)
   - sampling_tag (mandatory for evidence sampling decisions; values: always, sampled, none)

2) Proof-of-exercise and high-risk flags
   - Any entitlement granting admin-level or data-export permissions must set sampling_tag=always and attach a proof_of_exercise reference. Proof objects can be small (signed justification blob) or larger (recording transcript stored off-band).

3) TTL semantics for activation windows
   - Activation windows are authoritative: if end_ts < now the runtime must refuse use; a late-evaluation path will emit an expired-usage event rather than permit the action.

Audit retention and tiering model (recommended defaults)
- Hot (0-90 days): full-fidelity events, proofs, and enriched context stored in primary logging cluster for fast query and incident response.
- Warm (91-365 days): event indices kept for search; proofs and large payloads archived to object storage but metadata remains.
- Cold (366-1095 days): sparse indices only (timestamps, actor, subject, entitlement_type). Retrieval requires a justified workflow (ticket + accountable owner).
- Archive (1096+ days): compressed bundle exports kept per-compliance requests for defined tenants/regions.

Minimum retention by evidence type
- Entitlement-change events: 365 days (default)
- Always-sampled proofs for high-risk grants: 365 days hot, 3 years archive depending on contract
- Expired-usage events (attempted use after end_ts): 365 days
- Audit export bundles used for e-discovery: per legal hold (variable)

SIEM export considerations
- Export shape must be compact and stable; avoid full-proof payloads on streaming channel. Use metadata-only event for streaming and provide a fetch-href to object store for the heavy proof.
- Batch strategy: group events into 60s windows with a max envelope of ~1MB per batch to respect SIEM ingestion rates. For high-volume tenants, enforce per-tenant rate-limits and sampling.
- Backpressure: if SIEM endpoint rejects exports, buffer to durable storage and surface alert to SRE and compliance. Provide a degraded-mode policy: if buffer > threshold, convert non-critical events to sampled form to protect throughput.

Event example (streaming-friendly)
- event_id: uuid-1234
- ts: 2026-02-28T13:24:01Z
- actor: svc:access-manager
- subject: user:joe@example.com
- entitlement_type: role
- prev_state: bound
- new_state: active
- activation_window_start: 2026-02-28T13:00:00Z
- activation_window_end: 2026-02-28T14:00:00Z
- reason: 'support-session: escalation for live debugging'
- evidence_refs: gs://audit-bucket/proofs/uuid-1234 (pointer)
- sampling_tag: always

Evidence automation and sampling policy
- Sampling tiers (automated):
  - Tier A (always): admin-level, data-exfiltration, cross-tenant operations -> sample rate = 100% proofs stored hot.
  - Tier B (probabilistic): support-level escalations and developer transient grants -> sample rate = 20% by default (configurable per-tenant).
  - Tier C (none): routine role/attribute binds that are low-risk -> metadata-only events, proof omitted.
- Sampling decisions made at change-time with a deterministic hash of (tenant, actor, event_id) so sampled subsets are reproducible across retries.

Operational rollout plan (staged)
Stage 0: Pilot (internal + select beta tenants)
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Emit events in parallel to existing audit stream and new RBAC-v2-stream (non-production).
- Acceptance criteria: no missing events, activation_window enforcement in test harness, SIEM export adapter passes ingestion for sample batch.
- Tasks: update SDKs, run migration simulator, create canary dashboards.

Stage 1: Controlled rollout (10% tenants by usage)
- Duration: 6 weeks
- Features: enforcement on new grants only, export to SIEM in metadata mode, sampling defaults applied.
- Acceptance criteria: error rate < 0.1%, SIEM lag < 2 minutes for hot events, storage cost within budget forecast.

Stage 2: Broad rollout (all tenants opt-in)
- Duration: 8 weeks
- Features: enforced activation windows for new and re-applied grants, warm retention applied, legal hold workflow enabled.
- Acceptance criteria: KPIs met (see below), no customer-impact incidents in 14-day window.

Stage 3: Default enforcement (all tenants)
- Duration: rolling
- Policy: activation windows become default for temporary grants; entitlement history durable and exported.

Rollback safety and fast-fail controls
- Feature flag gating at control-plane and tenant-level.
- Instant rollback action: flip control-plane flag to ignore activation windows for a tenant (logs marked as degraded-mode).
- Evidence safeguard: on rollback, snapshot current entitlement state and push an archival evidence bundle to object store.

KPIs and monitoring
- Event completeness: percentage of entitlement changes that emit required canonical fields (>99.9% target).
- SIEM ingestion success rate: >99% per-batch success.
- Alert on sampling drift: number of Tier A events marked sampled!=always.
- Latency: time from event emission to SIEM ingestion (median < 90s hot path).

Acceptance tests (smoke)
- Create a time-bound grant with start_ts in the future: ensure grant is not usable before start_ts and audit shows scheduled activation.
- Create grant with end_ts in the past: ensure action is rejected and expired-usage event is emitted.
- High-risk grant: ensure sampling_tag=always and proof_ref is present.
- SIEM export test: send a 60s batch with mixed events and verify resulting indexable fields in test SIEM instance.

Open questions and TODOs
- Regional retention requirements: need mapping of legal/regional minima (EU, UK, US, APAC) and per-contract overrides. (Owner: Priya)
- Cost model: expected storage and SIEM egress costs for 100K events/day baseline. (Owner: Marcus)
- Proof storage encryption-at-rest control-plane contract with infra team (HLD required). (Owner: Ravi)
- UI/Console: how to display activation windows and proof download UX for customer security admins. (Owner: Elena)

Appendix: quick checklist for eng rollout
- [ ] Instrument entitlement-change emitter with canonical fields.
- [ ] Implement sampling hash function and config store toggle.
- [ ] Add batcher with 60s sliding window and size cap.
- [ ] Add backpressure buffer with alerting thresholds.
- [ ] Provide migration tool to backfill entitlement epochs for pilot tenants.
- [ ] Draft customer opt-in messaging and support playbook.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive for a 1st cut. Focus reviewer attention on: sampling defaults, retention durations, and fail-open rollback semantics.
- Expect follow-up PRD for console UX and a separate legal review for retention policy language."
